newsitem.title: USA: Bull U.S. unit charged with discrimination.
newsitem.headline: Bull U.S. unit charged with discrimination.

text.p: U.S. and state officials Thursday charged Bull HN, a unit of the French computer giant Cie des Machines Bull, with discriminating against workers aged 40 and older.

The Massachusetts attorney general and the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) filed complaints in federal court charging the software maker illegally required older, laid-off workers to forfeit their rights to pursue discrimination charges against the company in order to receive substantial severance pay and retirement packages.

"It is against the law to discriminate against older workers, and it is against the law to coerce them into agreements that discourage them from exercising their civil rights," Massachusetts Attorney General Scott Harshbarger said in a statement.
The company did not return phone calls seeking comment.

Meanwhile, the law enforcement agencies also maintain that Bull's severance paln falls short of federal law by not providing sufficient information, not giving workers sufficient time to consider its terms and not providing additional compensation.

Harshbarger, in his original probe of the Billerica, Mass.-based company, had alleged that Bull HN intentionally got rid of older, experienced workers in positions at all levels of the corporation, while hiring younger, inexperienced and less qualified workers.
